attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He describes Fraser's example but makes the mechanism claim in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the general denial that LLMs reason and limits the retrieval point to the one riddle case. Part of it is really a claim about an internal mechanism, but filing it as an observation is acceptable.

contract.note: The contract rightly says that 'reasoning' is undefined and contested, and that the mechanism behind one output of a closed model cannot be observed. Treating the claim as not adjudicable does not stretch it for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: The 2024 study (Wu et al., NAACL) predates the post and is relevant. It finds both reliance on familiar patterns and some abstract skill, so which way it cuts depends on how 'reasoning' is defined. Context only.

reviews.rationale: With no agreed definition of reasoning, 'literally don't' cannot be tested. The specific output and its mechanism are documented only in the speaker's own post. The study in the packet is mixed and serves as context only.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence summing up his point. It follows a quote from Phil Libin, but this sentence is his own conclusion.

semantics.note: The proposition drops 'short-term' and 'outside the box thinking', but the core evaluative claim survives. In substance it is a value judgment framed as an observation.

contract.note: No measure of 'genuine novelty' exists, and there is no baseline for an unbiased allocation, so the not-adjudicable framing is fair.

evidence.note: Crunchbase data on the 2024 AI funding split covers the full year rather than July 2024, and it cannot measure bias against novelty. Context only.

reviews.rationale: 'Hugely biased against genuine novelty' is an evaluative judgment with no agreed metric or baseline. Funding-share data shows where the money went, not whether investors were biased.

attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person forecast ('I fully expect').

semantics.note: 'Fully expect' signals unqualified expectation, so this is a scored forecast. The 12-month horizon is correctly set to 2025-07-28.

contract.note: Reading 'begin to burst' as the start of a broad, sustained unwinding of investment and valuations is an ordinary reading. It rightly excludes temporary selloffs and isolated failures, and it is not stretched for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: EY measured first-half 2025 GenAI VC investment that already exceeded the 2024 total, within the window and published before the cutoff. The fall in deal count reflects concentration, not contraction.
S&P webinar page dated July 15, 2025, reporting record quarterly funding and capital that is not slowing. Qualitative and promotional, but it corroborates continued momentum near the deadline.

reviews.rationale: The deadline has passed. Measured sector investment hit a record in the first half of 2025, and contemporaneous reporting near the deadline describes continued momentum. The temporary selloff around DeepSeek does not meet the bar for a sustained broad reversal. The contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: The opening line of Marcus's own post.

semantics.note: 'Will soon flame out' is a firm forecast. 'Soon' gives no definite deadline. The 'won't completely disappear' caveat is kept in the contract.

contract.note: Reading 'flame out' as a substantial, sustained collapse in adoption and commercial activity is fair. Declining to turn 'soon' into a deadline follows the open-horizon policy, though it is generous to the speaker.

evidence.note: OpenAI is describing its own product, so this is a company disclosure, not an independent finding. It reports growing adoption to mid-2026 and weighs against a collapse, but it cannot settle an open horizon.

Independent Reuters Institute survey showing weekly generative AI use rising from 18% to 34% between 2024 and 2025. It weighs against a collapse in that period, but not conclusively, given the open horizon.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the early-resolution rule needs evidence of an actual sustained collapse, which the packet does not show. Adoption kept growing through 2025–2026, which weighs against fulfilment, but under the contract that growth cannot conclusively refute an open-horizon forecast.
